title: Temurah 17
description: The end of chapter 2: unwitting substitution counts while unwitting consecration does not, Rabbi Elazar’s five animals that neither become sacred nor sanctify, Rava’s three tries at comparing them to a non-kosher animal, and Shmuel on a consecrated tereifa; then chapter 3 opens with the offspring and substitutes of peace offerings “until the end of all time.”
topics: ⚠️ “Shall be holy”: substitution done unwittingly counts, consecration does not
🔄 Ḥizkiyya, Reish Lakish and Rabbi Yoḥanan, black for white, and Rav Sheshet’s absent-minded vow: what unwitting substitution looks like
🚫 Rabbi Elazar’s five animals that neither become sacred nor sanctify, and Rabbi Meir’s “where would you find it?”
🐖 Like a non-kosher animal: Rava’s three tries, Rav Pappa’s tereifa and Rav Adda’s “too long or closed”
🐕 A tereifa consecrated: Shmuel’s “sanctified to die” against Rabbi Oshaya’s “wood and stones”
📖 Hadran: chapter 2, Yesh BaKorbanot, ends; chapter 3, Elu Kodashim, begins
♾️ Offspring of peace offerings “until the end of all time”: “if male, if female”, Rav Safra and Abaye, sacrifice or graze
🏛️ “Only your holy things”: Rabbi Yishmael and Rabbi Akiva on which offspring and substitutes are sacrificed

a1.he: לִיגָּזֵז וְלֵיעָבֵד. רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: עָשָׂה שׁוֹגֵג כְּמֵזִיד בַּתְּמוּרָה, וְלֹא עָשָׂה שׁוֹגֵג כְּמֵזִיד בַּמּוּקְדָּשִׁין.

a2.he: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: הַכִּלְאַיִם, וְהַטְּרֵפָה, וְהַיּוֹצֵא דּוֹפֶן, וְטוּמְטוּם, וְאַנְדְּרוֹגִינוֹס — לֹא קְדוֹשִׁין, וְלֹא מַקְדִּישִׁין.

a3.he: גְּמָ׳ מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה? אָמַר קְרָא ״יִהְיֶה קֹּדֶשׁ״, לְרַבּוֹת שׁוֹגֵג כְּמֵזִיד.

a4.he: הֵיכִי דָמֵי שׁוֹגֵג כְּמֵזִיד? אָמַר חִזְקִיָּה: כְּסָבוּר שֶׁהוּא מוּתָּר לְהָמִיר. גַּבֵּי תְּמוּרָה — לָקֵי, גַּבֵּי קָדָשִׁים — לָא לָקֵי.

a5.he: לִישָּׁנָא אַחֲרִינָא: גַּבֵּי תְּמוּרָה — קָדֵישׁ, גַּבֵּי קָדָשִׁים — לָא קָדֵישׁ.

a6.he: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמְרִי: כְּסָבוּר לוֹמַר ״תְּמוּרַת עוֹלָה״, וְאָמַר ״תְּמוּרַת שְׁלָמִים״. לִישָּׁנָא אַחֲרִינָא: גַּבֵּי תְּמוּרַת שְׁלָמִים — קָדֵישׁ, גַּבֵּי קָדָשִׁים — לָא קָדֵישׁ.

a7.he: לִישָּׁנָא אַחְרִינָא, כְּסָבוּר לוֹמַר ״שָׁחוֹר״ וְאָמַר ״לָבָן״ — גַּבֵּי תְּמוּרָה לָקֵי, גַּבֵּי קָדָשִׁים לָא לָקֵי.

a8.he: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: בְּאוֹמֵר ״תֵּצֵא זוֹ וְתִיכָּנֵס זוֹ״. גַּבֵּי קָדָשִׁים, בְּאוֹמֵר שֶׁנּוֹלַד בָּהֶם מוּם נֶאֱכָלִין בְּלֹא פִּדְיוֹן — לָא לָקֵי, גַּבֵּי תְּמוּרָה — לָקֵי.

a9.he: רַב שֵׁשֶׁת אָמַר: בְּאוֹמֵר ״אֶכָּנֵס לַבַּיִת זֶה וְאַקְדִּישׁ״ וְאָמִיר מִדַּעְתִּי, וְנִכְנַס וְהֵמִיר וְהִקְדִּישׁ שֶׁלֹּא מִדַּעְתּוֹ — גַּבֵּי תְּמוּרָה לָקֵי, גַּבֵּי קָדָשִׁים לָא לָקֵי.

a10.he: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: הַכִּלְאַיִם וְהַטְּרֵפָה וְכוּ׳. אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: לֹא קְדוֹשִׁין בִּתְמוּרָה, וְלֹא מַקְדִּישִׁין לַעֲשׂוֹת תְּמוּרָה.

a11.he: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר: וּמֵאַחַר שֶׁאֵין קְדוֹשִׁין, מֵהֵיכָן מַקְדִּישִׁין? אֶלָּא אִי אַתָּה מוֹצֵא אֶלָּא בְּמַקְדִּישׁ בְּהֵמָה וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִטְרְפָה, בְּמַקְדִּישׁ וָלָד וְיָצָא [דֶּרֶךְ] דּוֹפֶן. אֲבָל כִּלְאַיִם וְטוּמְטוּם וְאַנְדְּרוֹגִינוֹס, אִי אַתָּה מוֹצֵא אֶלָּא בְּוַלְדֵי קָדָשִׁים, וְאַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה דְּאָמַר: הַוָּלָד עוֹשֶׂה תְּמוּרָה.

a12.he: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר? כִּבְהֵמָה טְמֵאָה — מָה בְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה לָא קָרְבָה וְלָא נָחֲתָא לַהּ קְדוּשַּׁת הַגּוּף, אַף הָנָךְ לָא קָרְבִי וְלָא נָחֲתָא לְהוּ קְדוּשַּׁת הַגּוּף.

a13.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְרָבָא: וַהֲרֵי בַּעַל מוּם, דְּלָא קָרֵיב, וְנָחֲתָא לֵיהּ קְדוּשַּׁת הַגּוּף! אֲמַר לֵיהּ: בַּעַל מוּם קָרֵב בְּמִינוֹ. אִי הָכִי, טְרֵפָה נָמֵי קָא קָרְבָה בְּמִינָהּ!

a14.he: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: כִּבְהֵמָה טְמֵאָה, מָה בְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה פְּסוּל הַגּוּף, אַף כֹּל פְּסוּל הַגּוּף, לְאַפּוֹקֵי בַּעַל מוּם דִּפְסוּל חִסָּרוֹן נִינְהוּ.

a15.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַדָּא לְרָבָא: וַהֲלֹא ״שָׂרוּעַ״ וְ״קָלוּט״ כְּתִיב בַּפָּרָשָׁה, וְהָא הָנֵי פְּסוּל הַגּוּף נִינְהוּ!

a16.he: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: כִּבְהֵמָה [טְמֵאָה], מָה בְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה דְּלֵיכָּא בְּמִינַהּ, אַף כֹּל דְּלֵיכָּא בְּמִינַהּ, לְאַפּוֹקֵי בַּעַל מוּם דְּהָא אִיכָּא בְּמִינַהּ.

a17.he: מַאי אָמְרַתְּ: טְרֵפָה אִיכָּא בְּמִינַהּ? לָא דָּמְיָא לְבַעַל מוּם, בְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה אֲסוּרָה בַּאֲכִילָה, וּטְרֵפָה אֲסוּרָה בַּאֲכִילָה, לְאַפּוֹקֵי בַּעַל מוּם דְּמוּתָּר בַּאֲכִילָה.

a18.he: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הַמַּקְדִּישׁ אֶת הַטְּרֵיפָה צְרִיכָה מוּם קָבוּעַ לִפְדּוֹת עָלָיו, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ פּוֹדִין אֶת הַקֳּדָשִׁים לְהַאֲכִילָן לִכְלָבִים?

a19.he: אֶלָּא אֵימָא: עוֹשָׂה קְדוּשָּׁה (לְמִיתָה, כְּסָבוּר מוּתָּר לְהַקְדִּישׁ בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין לְגַבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ, גַּבֵּי תְּמוּרָה — קָדֵישׁ, גַּבֵּי קָדָשִׁים — לָא קָדֵישׁ) לָמוּת, וְרַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא אוֹמֵר: אֵינָהּ אֶלָּא כְּמַקְדִּישׁ עֵצִים וַאֲבָנִים בִּלְבַד.

a20.he: תְּנַן: כָּל הַקֳּדָשִׁים שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ טְרֵפָה, אֵין פּוֹדִין אוֹתָן, לְפִי שֶׁאֵין פּוֹדִין הַקֳּדָשִׁים לְהַאֲכִילָן לִכְלָבִים. טַעְמָא שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ, הָא הָיוּ מֵעִיקָּרָא — פּוֹדִין אוֹתָן! דִּלְמָא הַאי תַּנָּא סָבַר: כֹּל הֵיכָא דְּלָא חֲזֵי לְגוּפַהּ, לָא נָחֲתָא לַהּ קְדוּשַּׁת הַגּוּף.

a21.he: תָּא שְׁמַע: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: הַכִּלְאַיִם, וְיוֹצֵא דוֹפֶן, וּטְרֵיפָה, וְטוּמְטוּם וְאַנְדְּרוֹגִינוֹס — לֹא קְדוֹשִׁין וְלֹא מַקְדִּישִׁין. וְאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: לֹא קְדוֹשִׁין בִּתְמוּרָה, וְלֹא מַקְדִּישִׁין לַעֲשׂוֹת תְּמוּרָה.

a22.he: וְתַנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר: וְכִי מֵאַחַר שֶׁאֵין קְדוֹשִׁין, מֵהֵיכָן מַקְדִּישִׁין? אֶלָּא אִי אַתָּה מוֹצֵא אֶלָּא בְּמַקְדִּישׁ בְּהֵמָה וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִטְרְפָה, הָא הָיְתָה טְרֵפָה מֵעִיקָּרָא — לָא נָחֲתָא לֵיהּ קְדוּשַּׁת הַגּוּף.

b1.he: אָמַר לְךָ שְׁמוּאֵל: דִּלְמָא הָךְ תַּנָּא נָמֵי סָבַר כֹּל הֵיכָא דְּלָא חַזְיָא לְגוּפַהּ — לָא נָחֲתָא לַהּ קְדוּשַּׁת הַגּוּף.

b3.he: מַתְנִי׳ אֵלּוּ קָדָשִׁים שֶׁוַּולְדוֹתֵיהֶן וּתְמוּרוֹתֵיהֶן כַּיּוֹצֵא בָּהֶן, וְלַד שְׁלָמִים וּתְמוּרָתָן, וְלָדָן וּוְלַד וְלָדָן עַד סוֹף כׇּל הָעוֹלָם — הֲרֵי הֵן שְׁלָמִים, וּטְעוּנִין סְמִיכָה וּנְסָכִים וּתְנוּפַת חָזֶה וָשׁוֹק.

b4.he: גְּמָ׳ כֵּיוָן דִּתְנָא ״וְלָדָן וּוְלַד וְלָדָן״, ״עַד סוֹף כׇּל הָעוֹלָם״ לְמָה לִי? תַּנָּא דִידַן שַׁמְעֵיהּ לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר דְּאָמַר ״וְלַד שְׁלָמִים לֹא יִקְרַב שְׁלָמִים״, וַאֲמַר לֵיהּ תַּנָּא דִידַן: לָא מִיבַּעְיָא בִּוְולָדָן דְּלָא מוֹדֵינָא, אֶלָּא אֲפִילּוּ עַד סוֹף הָעוֹלָם לָא מוֹדֵינָא לָךְ.

b5.he: מְנָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי? דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״זָכָר״ — לְרַבּוֹת אֶת הַוָּלָד.

b6.he: וַהֲלֹא דִין הוּא: וּמָה תְּמוּרָה, שֶׁאֵין גִּידּוּלֵי הֶקְדֵּשׁ — קְרֵיבָה, וָלָד, שֶׁגִּידּוּלֵי הֶקְדֵּשׁ — אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁיִּקְרַב?

b7.he: מָה לִתְמוּרָה, שֶׁכֵּן נוֹהֶגֶת בְּכׇל הַקֳּדָשִׁים, תֹּאמַר בְּוָלָד, שֶׁאֵינוֹ נוֹהֵג בְּכׇל הַקֳּדָשִׁים? אֵינוֹ קָרֵב הוֹאִיל וְאֵינוֹ נוֹהֵג בְּכׇל הַקֳּדָשִׁים. תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״זָכָר״ — לְרַבּוֹת אֶת הַוָּלָד, ״נְקֵבָה״ — לְרַבּוֹת הַתְּמוּרָה.

b8.he: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא תְּמוּרַת תְּמִימִין, וּוְלַד תְּמִימִין, וְלַד בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין וּתְמוּרַת בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין מִנַּיִן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״אִם זָכָר״ לְרַבּוֹת וְלַד בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין, ״אִם נְקֵבָה״ לְרַבּוֹת תְּמוּרַת בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין.

b9.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב סָפְרָא לְאַבָּיֵי: וְאֵיפוֹךְ אֲנָא! מִסְתַּבְּרָא, מִמָּקוֹם שֶׁנִּתְרַבְּתָה תְּמוּרַת תְּמִימִין נִתְרַבְּתָה תְּמוּרַת בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין.

b10.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִי קָאָמֵינָא לָךְ לֵיפוֹךְ ״אִם זָכָר״ ״אִם נְקֵבָה״? אֲנָא כּוּלֵּיהּ קְרָא קָאָמֵינָא! אֵימָא: ״זָכָר״ לְרַבּוֹת אֶת הַתְּמוּרָה, ״נְקֵבָה״ לְרַבּוֹת אֶת הַוָּלָד. אֲמַר לֵיהּ: ״וָלָד״ לְשׁוֹן זָכָר מַשְׁמַע, ״תְּמוּרָה״ לְשׁוֹן נְקֵבָה מַשְׁמַע.

b11.he: לְמַאי הִלְכְתָא? אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: לִיקְרַב, וְאַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר.

b12.he: דְּמַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: כִּי קָאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר עוֹלָה, דְּאִיכָּא שֵׁם עוֹלָה עַל אִמּוֹ, אֲבָל הָנֵי וְלָדוֹת לָא קָרְבִי — קָמַשְׁמַע לַן.

b13.he: בַּר פְּדָא אָמַר: לִרְעִיָּה, וְאַלִּיבָּא דְּדִבְרֵי הַכֹּל. דְּאִתְּמַר: רָבָא אָמַר: לִיקְרַב, וְאַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר. רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: לִרְעִיָּה, וְאַלִּיבָּא דְּדִבְרֵי הַכֹּל.

b15.he: ״רָק קֳדָשֶׁיךָ״ — אֵלּוּ תְּמוּרוֹת, ״אֲשֶׁר יִהְיוּ לָךְ״ — אֵלּוּ הַוְּולָדוֹת, ״תִּשָּׂא וּבָאת״.

b16.he: יָכוֹל יַכְנִיסֶנּוּ לְבֵית הַבְּחִירָה, וְיִמְנַע מֵהֶם מַיִם וּמָזוֹן כְּדֵי שֶׁיָּמוּתוּ? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״וְעָשִׂיתָ עוֹלוֹתֶיךָ הַבָּשָׂר וְהַדָּם״, כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאַתָּה נוֹהֵג בְּעוֹלָה — אַתָּה נוֹהֵג בִּתְמוּרָה, כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאַתָּה נוֹהֵג בִּשְׁלָמִים — אַתָּה נוֹהֵג בְּוַולְדֵי שְׁלָמִים וּבִתְמוּרָה.

b17.he: יָכוֹל כׇּל קָדָשִׁים כֵּן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״רַק״ — דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל. רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ, הֲרֵי הוּא אוֹמֵר ״אָשָׁם הוּא אָשֹׁם אָשַׁם לַה׳״ — הוּא קָרֵב, וְאֵין תְּמוּרָתוֹ קְרֵיבָה.

b18.he: אָמַר מָר: ״תִּשָּׂא וּבָאת״, יָכוֹל יַכְנִיסֶנּוּ לְבֵית הַבְּחִירָה?

b19.he: מְנָא תֵּיתֵי הָא? כֵּיוָן דְּגָמְרִי חָמֵשׁ חַטָּאוֹת, הָנָךְ מִקְרָב קָרְבִי!

b20.he: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: חָמֵשׁ חַטָּאוֹת מֵתוֹת בְּכׇל מָקוֹם, וְהָנָךְ יָמוּתוּ בְּבֵית הַבְּחִירָה — קָמַשְׁמַע לַן.

b21.he: אָמַר מָר: יָכוֹל אַף כָּל הַקֳּדָשִׁים כֵּן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״רַק קָדָשֶׁיךָ״. וָלָד דְּמַאן? אִי דְּעוֹלָה — זָכָר הוּא, וְלָאו בַּר אוֹלוֹדֵי הוּא! וְאִי דְּחַטָּאת — גְּמִירִי לַהּ דִּלְמִיתָה קָיְימִי!

messages.text: Continued from 16b: the mishna lists where substitution is more stringent than consecration. Substitution imbues even an animal with a permanent blemish with inherent sanctity, and blemished animals consecrated through substitution do not emerge to non-sacred status through redemption…
Mishna
…in terms of it being permitted to shear its wool and to perform labor with it.

notes.he: אלא כדין קדשים שקדם הקדשן את מומן שכשפודין אותן אין בהן היתר גיזה ועבודה אלא היתר אכילה כדאמרי' בפ' שני דבכורות (דף יד.) משא"כ בקדשים שאם קדם מומן להקדשן יוצאין לחולין ע"י פדיון ליגזז וליעבד כדאמרי' התם בבכורות אבל בתמורה גלי קרא (ויקרא כ״ז:י׳) טוב ברע או רע בטוב לא הפריש בין תם לבעל מום:
notes.en: To be shorn and to be worked: [they do not go out to non-sacred status with permission to be shorn and worked,] but only like the law of sacrificial animals whose consecration preceded their blemish, which, when they are redeemed, have no permission for shearing and labor but only permission to be eaten, as we say in the second chapter of Bekhorot (14a). This is not so with sacrificial animals whose blemish preceded their consecration, which go out to non-sacred status through redemption, to be shorn and to be worked, as we say there in Bekhorot. But with regard to substitution the verse revealed (Leviticus 27:10) “a good for a bad, or a bad for a good”: it did not distinguish between an unblemished animal and a blemished one.

messages.text: There is an additional stringency that applies to substitution but not to consecration: The Torah rendered the status of one who acts unwittingly like that of one who acts intentionally with regard to substitution, as in both cases the substitute is consecrated. But it did not render the status of one who acts unwittingly like that of one who acts intentionally with regard to consecrated items, since unwitting consecration is ineffective.

notes.he: עשה שוגג כמזיד בתמורה ולא בקדשים:
notes.en: He rendered unwitting like intentional with regard to substitution, but not with regard to sacrificial animals.

messages.text: An animal crossbred from diverse kinds, and a tereifa, and an animal born by caesarean section, and a tumtum animal, and a hermaphrodite animal are not sacred through consecration, and if they were sacred beforehand, e.g., one consecrated an animal and it subsequently became a tereifa, they do not sanctify non-sacred animals by means of substitution.
Gemara
What is the reason for the opinion of Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, that substitution applies whether one substitutes unwittingly or intentionally?
messages.quote: The Torah rendered the status of one who acts unwittingly like that of one who acts intentionally with regard to substitution

messages.text: The verse states: “He shall not alter it, nor substitute it, a good for a bad, or a bad for a good; and if he shall substitute his animal for an animal, then both it and that for which it is changed shall be holy.” The apparently superfluous term “shall be” serves to include the case of one who acts unwittingly like that of one who acts intentionally, with regard to substitution.

verse.he: לֹא יַחֲלִיפֶנּוּ וְלֹא־יָמִיר אֹתוֹ טוֹב בְּרָע אוֹ־רַע בְּטוֹב וְאִם־הָמֵר יָמִיר בְּהֵמָה בִּבְהֵמָה וְהָיָה־הוּא וּתְמוּרָתוֹ יִהְיֶה־קֹּדֶשׁ׃
verse.en: One may not exchange or substitute another for it, either good for bad, or bad for good; if one does substitute one animal for another, the thing vowed and its substitute shall both be holy.

messages.text: What are the circumstances in which one who acts unwittingly is considered like one who acts intentionally with regard to substitution?

The circumstances are of one who thinks that it is permitted to substitute one animal for another. With regard to a substitute, the animal becomes consecrated, and the individual is liable to receive lashes for transgressing the Torah’s prohibition, due to the inclusion of “shall be,” despite the fact that he acted unwittingly.

notes.he: דרבי ביה קרא הוא שוגג כמזיד:
notes.en: GEMARA. With regard to a substitute he is flogged: for the verse included in it unwitting like intentional.

notes.he: דהא כתיב יהיה קדש לרבות שוגג כמזיד:
notes.en: With regard to substitution he is flogged: for it is written “shall be holy,” to include unwitting like intentional.

messages.text: But in the equivalent case, where one unwittingly sanctified an animal that was unfit to be an offering, he is not liable to receive lashes, as in this case one is liable to receive lashes only if he acted intentionally and with prior warning.

notes.he: דלא מצינו מלקות אלא במזיד ובהתראה:
notes.en: With regard to sacrificial animals he is not flogged: for we do not find lashes except for one who acts intentionally and with forewarning.

notes.dh: גבי תמורה לקי גבי קדשים לא לקי
notes.he: ואית ספרים דגרסי גבי תמורה קדיש כו' ולפי גי' ראשונה משום דשוגג דתמורה לקי דגזירת הכתוב היא משום דכתיב יהיה לרבות שוגג כמזיד ורבינו ברוך ורבינו שמעון שאנץ איפלגו בה הרבה אם יש מלקות בשוגג דתמורה ומצאו בה ספרים חלוקים הכא ובריש מכילתין פירשתיו ומיהו בסמוך גבי כסבור קדשים שנולד להם מום נאכלין בלא פדיון לא מצינו למגרס גבי קדשים לא קדש שהרי קדוש ועומד הוא מעיקרא אלא ה"ג ביה גבי תמורה לקי גבי קדשים לא לקי:
notes.en: With regard to substitution he is flogged; with regard to sacrificial animals he is not flogged: And some books read: “With regard to substitution it is consecrated,” etc. According to the first reading, the reason one who substitutes unwittingly is flogged is that it is a decree of the verse, since “shall be” is written, to include unwitting like intentional. Rabbeinu Barukh and Rabbeinu Shimon of Sens disagreed about this at length, whether there are lashes for unwitting substitution, and they found divergent books here; and I explained it at the beginning of our tractate. However, shortly below, in the case of one who thinks that sacrificial animals that developed a blemish are eaten without redemption, we cannot read “with regard to sacrificial animals it is not consecrated,” since it was already consecrated from the outset. Rather, this is how we read there: “With regard to substitution he is flogged; with regard to sacrificial animals he is not flogged.”

notes.he: אם שוגג (הוא) אבל המקדיש בעל מום קבוע במזיד עובר בה' לאוין כדאמרן בפרק קמא:
notes.en: And with regard to sacrificial animals he is not flogged: if he acted unwittingly. But one who consecrates an animal with a permanent blemish intentionally transgresses five prohibitions, as we said in the first chapter.

messages.text: With regard to a non-sacred animal that was declared a substitute, the animal becomes consecrated, despite the fact that one acted unwittingly. But with regard to sacrificial animals, if it was consecrated unwittingly it is not consecrated.
messages.lead: The Gemara cites an alternative version of Ḥizkiyya’s statement:

messages.text: The case is of one who thinks to say: This animal shall be a substitute for a burnt offering that I own, but he unwittingly said: This animal shall be a substitute for a peace offering that I own. In such a case involving substitution he is liable to receive lashes, but if he erred in this manner with regard to consecration, he is exempt from lashes.

With regard to a substitute of a peace offering, if one unwittingly declared it a substitute, it is consecrated. With regard to sacrificial animals, if the animal was unwittingly consecrated, it is not consecrated.
messages.lead: The Gemara cites an alternative version:

messages.text: Another alternative version of the difference between substitution and consecration of an animal: The case is of one who thinks to say: The first black animal that comes out of my house will be a substitute, but he unwittingly said: The first white animal that comes out of my house will be a substitute. With regard to a substitute, the white animal is consecrated, and the individual therefore is liable to receive lashes for transgressing the Torah’s prohibition, despite the fact that he acted unwittingly.

notes.he: שור שחור שיצא מביתי תחלה יהא תמורה תחת זה ויצא מפיו שור לבן גבי תמורה קדיש ולקי דגלי ביה קרא:
notes.en: He thought to say: The black ox that comes out of my house first shall be a substitute in place of this one, and there came out of his mouth “white ox.” With regard to substitution it is consecrated and he is flogged, for the verse revealed it.

notes.he: להקדיש אדום והקדיש שחור לא קדיש כדתנן הקדש טעות בש"א הקדש ובה"א אינו הקדש:
notes.en: He thought: to consecrate a red one, and he consecrated a black one [the Davidson English reads black and white]. It is not consecrated, as we learned: consecration in error, Beit Shammai say it is consecration and Beit Hillel say it is not consecration.

messages.text: Conversely, in a similar case of sacrificial animals, e.g., one meant to say: The first blemished black animal that comes out of my house shall be consecrated, but he unwittingly said: The first blemished white animal shall be consecrated, if a white animal came out of his house, the animal is not consecrated, and therefore he is not liable to receive lashes.

notes.he: אם בעל מום הוא למזבח לא לקי דהא לא קדיש דהקדש טעות אינו הקדש:
notes.en: With regard to sacrificial animals: if it is a blemished animal [consecrated] for the altar, he is not flogged, since it is not consecrated at all, for consecration in error is not consecration.

messages.text: Another case of unwitting substitution of an animal: This is referring to a case of one who says: Let this animal emerge from its sanctity and become non-sacred, and let that animal enter in its place and become consecrated. This person acted unwittingly, because he mistakenly thought that in this manner the consecrated animal would no longer be sacred.

notes.he: ואותה של הקדש תמימה היא ולא נפקא לחולין אלא תופסת זו בקדושתה והויא תמורה והוא סבור שתצא לחולין כבעל מום ולא להמיר נתכוין ואפ"ה לקי וגבי קדשים נמי דומיא דהאי שהיה יודע שהקדשים אסורין לזרים אבל סבר הוא דהיכא דנפל בהן מום נאכלין בלא פדיון והיינו דומיא דהאי שהיה יודע שהתמורה אסורה אבל בכי האי גוונא סבר דמותר:
notes.en: Let this one go out and let that one enter: and that consecrated animal is unblemished and does not go out to non-sacred status; rather, this one is caught up in its sanctity and becomes a substitute. He thought that it would go out to non-sacred status like a blemished animal, and he did not intend to substitute, and even so he is flogged. And with regard to sacrificial animals, too, it is a case similar to this: he knew that sacrificial animals are forbidden to non-priests, but he thought that where a blemish befell them they are eaten without redemption. That is similar to this one, who knew that substitution is forbidden but thought that in such a manner it is permitted.

notes.dh: כגון דאמר תצא זו לחולין ותכנס זו תמורה בקדושתה
notes.he: גבי תמורה לקי כדאמרן בפ"ק לא יחליפנו בשל אחרים שאינו שלו דהיינו תצא שלי (זו) לחולין ותהא של פלוני [ואותה שלו תהא] תמורתה קדשה ולקי דהוי תמורה:
notes.en: Such as where he said: Let this one go out to non-sacred status and let that one enter as a substitute in its sanctity. With regard to substitution he is flogged, as we said in the first chapter: “He shall not exchange it,” with others’ animals that are not his; that is: let mine go out to non-sacred status and be so-and-so’s, and that one of his shall be its substitute. It is consecrated and he is flogged, for it is substitution.

messages.text: With regard to a similar case involving sacrificial animals, where he has a sacrificial animal that developed a blemish and he incorrectly says: Any animals that have developed a blemish may be eaten without redemption, and he proceeded to eat the animal without first redeeming it, he is not liable to receive lashes. But with regard to a substitute, if he did this he would be liable to receive lashes, as stated above.

notes.he: לא לקי דלא כתיב בהו יהיה:
notes.en: With regard to sacrificial animals: he is not flogged, for “shall be” is not written about them.

messages.text: Yet another example of unwittingly performing substitution: It is referring to a case of one who says: I will enter this house and consecrate an animal intentionally, or: I will enter this house and substitute an animal intentionally, and he entered and substituted or consecrated unintentionally, i.e., he acted absentmindedly.

notes.he: שבעל מחשבות הוא ולא היה יודע מה היה אומר בתמורה קדשי ולקי דגלי קרא שוגג כמזיד:
notes.en: And he entered and consecrated and substituted without his awareness: for he is a man lost in his thoughts and did not know what he was saying. With regard to substitution it is consecrated and he is flogged, for the verse revealed unwitting like intentional.

notes.dh: אכנס לבית זה כו' הקדיש שלא מדעתו
notes.he: פרש"י שבעל מחשבות היה ולא היה יודע מה היה אומר וקשה למה לו לומר אכנס לבית כו' לכך נראה לפרש אכנס לבית זה כו' כלומר כשאכנס לבית זה תהיה בהמה זו תמורה מיד וזו תהיה קדושה מדעתיה ונכנס בה והמיר והקדיש שלא מדעתו שלא אמר דבר בכניסתו וגם לא חשב במה שאמר מתחילה ונמצא שחל התמורה וההקדש שלא מדעת:
notes.en: “I will enter this house, etc.,” and he consecrated without his awareness: Rashi explained that he was a man lost in his thoughts and did not know what he was saying. And this is difficult: why does he need to say “I will enter this house,” etc.? Therefore it seems right to explain “I will enter this house,” etc., as meaning: When I enter this house, this animal shall at once be a substitute and that one shall be consecrated, with my awareness. And he entered it, and substituted and consecrated without his awareness, for he said nothing upon entering and also did not think about what he had said at first; it turns out that the substitution and the consecration took effect without his awareness.

messages.text: For his transgression with regard to substitution he is liable to receive lashes, and for his transgression with regard to sacrificial animals he is not liable to receive lashes.

notes.he: לא קדיש ואי איכא בעל מום למזבח לא לקי דהא לא קדיש דהקדש טעות הוא:
notes.en: With regard to sacrificial animals: it is not consecrated, and if it is a blemished animal [consecrated] for the altar, he is not flogged, since it is not consecrated, for it is consecration in error.

messages.text: § The mishna taught that Rabbi Elazar says: An animal crossbred from diverse kinds, and a tereifa, and an animal born by caesarean section, and a tumtum animal, and a hermaphrodite animal, are neither sacred through consecration nor do they sanctify non-sacred animals by means of substitution.

They are not sanctified by substitution, i.e., if one said that an animal in any of these categories should be a substitute for a sacrificial animal, it does not become sanctified. And the clause that they do not sanctify non-sacred animals means that if one of these types of animal was sanctified and one attempted to render a non-sacred animal a substitute for it, that non-sacred animal does not become sanctified.
messages.lead: In explanation:

notes.he: אע"פ שהתמורה חלה קדושת הגוף על בעל מום קבוע אינה חלה על אלו וכ"ש שאין קדושת הגוף חלה עליהן בהקדש הפה אלא קדושת דמים כעצים ואבנים ואינן צריכין מום לפדות:
notes.en: They are not sanctified through substitution: even though with substitution inherent sanctity takes effect on an animal with a permanent blemish, it does not take effect on these. All the more so, inherent sanctity does not take effect on them through consecration by speech, but only sanctity of value, like wood and stones, and they do not require a blemish to be redeemed.

notes.he: אחרים בתמורה אם קדש הן:
notes.en: And they do not sanctify: others through substitution, if they are consecrated.

messages.text: But since these animals do not become sanctified, how can it even be suggested that they could sanctify another non-sacred animal? Rather, you find that the ruling of Rabbi Elazar applies only when one sanctifies an animal and afterward it became a tereifa, or when one sanctifies a fetus and it emerged from the womb by caesarean section.
messages.lead: It is taught in a baraita that

notes.he: ור' מאיר מפרש היאך הן קדושין שצריך לומר שאין מקדישין:
notes.en: And Rabbi Meir explains how they can be consecrated, such that it needs to be said that they do not sanctify.

notes.he: דחיילא עלה קדושה:
notes.en: In one who consecrates an animal: on which sanctity takes effect.

notes.he: (אע"פ קדושה היא) בזו הוצרך לומר שאף על פי שקדושה היא אינו עושה תמורה אבל כלאים וטומטום ואנדרוגינוס מתחילת ברייתן נתקלקלו ואין בהן אותה קדושה:
notes.en: And afterward it became a tereifa: (even though it is consecrated). In this case it was necessary to say that even though it is consecrated, it does not effect substitution. But diverse kinds, a tumtum and a hermaphrodite were spoiled from the outset of their creation and do not have that sanctity.

messages.text: But with regard to an animal crossbred from diverse kinds, and a tumtum, and a hermaphrodite, you can find this ruling only in a case of the offspring of consecrated female animals, which have sanctity without an act of consecration. And this is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda, who said that the offspring of a consecrated animal renders a non-sacred animal that is exchanged for it consecrated as a substitute.

notes.he: שקדשה אמן קודם שנתעברה דהשתא ממילא הן קדושים דעובר ירך אמו הוא ובהא הוצרך לומר דאינן עושין תמורה:
notes.en: Only in the offspring of sacrificial animals: whose mother was consecrated before she became pregnant, for then they are consecrated of themselves, since a fetus is like the thigh of its mother. And in this case it was necessary to say that they do not effect substitution.

notes.he: בשאר ולד קדשים עושה תמורה איצטריך לאשמועינן בהני דלא עבדי תמורה ולא נחתא להו קדושת הגוף אפילו ע"י תמורה והני דאמרן לאו רע מעיקרו נינהו דהא אוקימנא במקדיש בהמה ואח"כ נטרפה במקדיש ולד כו' וטומטום ואנדרוגינוס קדשי אגב אמן קודם יצירתן:
notes.en: And according to Rabbi Yehuda, who said: that with other offspring of sacrificial animals the offspring effects substitution, it was necessary to teach us about these that they do not effect substitution and that inherent sanctity does not take effect on them even through substitution. And the ones we mentioned are not “bad from the outset” [i.e., blemished before they were consecrated], for we established it as one who consecrates an animal and afterward it became a tereifa, one who consecrates a fetus, etc.; and the tumtum and the hermaphrodite are consecrated by virtue of their mother before they were formed.

notes.he: אי אתה מוצא אלא בוולדי קדשים דקדשי אגב אימיהו]. וכר' יהודה דאמר בשאר וולדות קדשים וולד עושה תמורה. אבל הני אין מקדישין לעשות [תמורה] דלא אלים קדושתיהו:
notes.en: It is taught: Rabbi Meir said: Since, etc., as we explained in the first chapter. You find it only in the offspring of sacrificial animals, which are consecrated by virtue of their mothers, and in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda, who said that with other offspring of sacrificial animals the offspring effects substitution. But these do not sanctify to effect substitution, for their sanctity is not strong.

messages.text: What is the reason for the opinion of Rabbi Elazar? He holds that the halakhot of these categories of animal is like that of a non-kosher domesticated animal: Just as a non-kosher domesticated animal is not sacrificed as an offering and inherent sanctity does not rest upon it, so too, these animals in the categories of a tereifa, an animal born by caesarean section, a tumtum, or a hermaphrodite may not be sacrificed as offerings and inherent sanctity does not rest upon them.

notes.he: קסבר דינן כבהמה טמאה:
notes.en: He holds that their law is like that of a non-kosher animal.

messages.text: As printed, this first explanation is Rav Pappa’s; in the exchange that follows Rav Pappa challenges Rava, and Rava’s next two explanations each begin “Rather.”
@Rava But why aren’t animals in these categories compared to a blemished animal, which may not be sacrificed as an offering but nevertheless inherent sanctity does rest upon it?

notes.dh: והרי בעל מום דלא קרב ונחתא ליה קדושת הגוף
notes.he: ע"י תמורה כדקתני מתני' שהתמורה חלה כו' ואי קדם הקדשו את מומו עביד תמורה כדכתיב טוב ברע והך בהמה נמי שקדם הקדשה את טריפתה תעביד תמורה ואי נטרפה כשהיתה חולין תתפוס בתמורה:
notes.en: But there is a blemished animal, which is not sacrificed, and inherent sanctity takes effect on it: through substitution, as the mishna teaches that substitution takes effect, etc. And if its consecration preceded its blemish, it effects substitution, as it is written: “a good for a bad.” So this animal too, whose consecration preceded its becoming a tereifa, should effect substitution; and if it became a tereifa while it was non-sacred, it should be caught up [in sanctity] through substitution.

notes.he: [והא קדיש קדושת הגוף] וקתני דתמורה חלה עליו ותמורה (היינו) [הוי] קדושת הגוף:
notes.en: But there is a blemished animal, which is not sacrificed, and yet it is consecrated with inherent sanctity, as it teaches that substitution takes effect on it, and substitution is inherent sanctity.

messages.text: Although a blemished animal is not sacrificed on the altar, another animal of its same type, i.e., an unblemished animal, is sacrificed as an offering. By contrast, an animal born by caesarean section, a tumtum, and a hermaphrodite may never be sacrificed.
messages.lead: Rava said to Rav Pappa in response:

notes.he: שאר בהמות תמימות אבל כל הני ה' לא קרבי במינו. יוצא דופן לא חשיב ליה מין שאר בהמות דתמיהו אנשי:
notes.en: Is sacrificed in its kind: other, unblemished animals. But all these five are not sacrificed in their kind. An animal born by caesarean section is not considered of the kind of other animals, for people would be astonished at it.

notes.he: בעל מום איכא במינו דקרב הילכך קדיש קדושת הגוף:
notes.en: A blemished animal has its kind that is sacrificed; therefore it is consecrated with inherent sanctity.

messages.text: If so, what will you say about a tereifa, as other animals of its type are sacrificed. According to your explanation, why doesn’t inherent sanctity rest upon a tereifa?
messages.lead: Rav Pappa said to Rava:

notes.dh: אי הכי טרפה נמי הא קרבה במינה
notes.he: אבל מן השאר לא פריך דטומטום ואנדרוגינוס בריות משונות הן והוי כאילו לא קרב במינן וכך יוצא דופן תהי בה אינשי והוי כאילו לא קרב במינו וכן כלאים משונה הוא והוי כאילו לא קרב במינו וכן פרש"י:
notes.en: If so, a tereifa too is sacrificed in its kind: But he does not raise a difficulty from the others, for a tumtum and a hermaphrodite are anomalous creatures, and it is as though their kind is not sacrificed. And so too, at an animal born by caesarean section people are astonished, and it is as though its kind is not sacrificed. And so too, diverse kinds are anomalous, and it is as though their kind is not sacrificed. And so Rashi explained.

messages.text: The halakhot of animals in these categories are like those of a non-kosher domesticated animal, in the following manner: Just as the category of a non-kosher domesticated animal is an inherent disqualification, and such an animal cannot be sanctified or render another animal sanctified, so too the same applies to any other category of animal that is an inherent disqualification, such as a tereifa, an animal born by caesarean section, a tumtum animal, and a hermaphrodite. This serves to exclude blemished animals, which are disqualified only because they lack certain limbs.
messages.lead: Rather, Rava retracts his previous answer and instead says:

notes.he: וכל הני פסול הגוף הן בלא חסרון כגון ניקב קרום של מוח וניקבה הקיבה אבל מום פסול חסרון בעלמא הוא:
notes.en: An inherent disqualification: and all of these are inherent disqualifications without anything lacking, such as a perforated membrane of the brain or a perforated abomasum. But a blemish is merely a disqualification of something lacking.

notes.he: כגון הללו כלאים וטרפה לא קדשי קדושת הגוף לאפוקי בעל מום דפסול חסרון אבר [הוא] וקדיש קדושת הגוף:
notes.en: So too any inherent disqualification, such as these, diverse kinds and a tereifa: they are not consecrated with inherent sanctity. To exclude a blemished animal, which is a disqualification of a lacking limb and is consecrated with inherent sanctity.

messages.text: @Rava Is the disqualification of a blemished animal always because it is lacking a limb? But isn’t the phrase: Too long or closed hooves, written in the passage of the Torah addressing blemishes that disqualify an animal; and these are inherent disqualifications. The verse states: “Either a bull or a lamb that has any limb too long or closed hooves, you may offer for a voluntary offering; but for a vow it shall not be accepted.”
messages.quote: to exclude blemished animals, which are disqualified only because they lack certain limbs

verse.he: וְשׁוֹר וָשֶׂה שָׂרוּעַ וְקָלוּט נְדָבָה תַּעֲשֶׂה אֹתוֹ וּלְנֵדֶר לֹא יֵרָצֶה׃
verse.en: You may, however, present as a freewill offering an ox or a sheep with a limb extended or contracted; but it will not be accepted for a vow.

notes.he: (ויקרא כ״ב:כ״ג) גבי בעלי מומין והני פסול הגוף נינהו בלא חסרון ואפי' הכי עביד תמורה דכתיב טוב ברע הכי פירש רבי:
notes.en: But isn’t “too long” and “closed” written in the passage (Leviticus 22:23) about blemished animals: and these are inherent disqualifications without anything lacking, and even so they effect substitution, as it is written: “a good for a bad.” So my teacher explained.

notes.he: והלא שרוע וקלוט [כתוב בפרשת בעלי מומין והללו] לית בהו חסרון דשרוע שנשתרבבה יריכו. קלוט שפרסותיו קלוטות כשל חמור דלאו פסול חסרון [אלא] פסולי הגוף נינהו כטרפה (והא) [וקא] קדשי קדושת הגוף כתמורה:
notes.en: But isn’t “too long” and “closed” written in the passage of blemished animals, and these have nothing lacking: for “too long” [sarua] is one whose thigh is extended, and “closed” [kalut] is one whose hooves are closed like those of a donkey. These are not disqualifications of something lacking but inherent disqualifications, like a tereifa, and yet they are consecrated with inherent sanctity, as with a substitute.

messages.text: The explanation of Rabbi Elazar’s opinion is as I explained initially. The halakhot of animals in these categories are like those of a non-kosher domesticated animal: Just as a non-kosher domesticated animal is not sacrificed on the altar and neither are any animals of its type, so too these halakhot apply to any animal that is not sacrificed on the altar and neither are any animals of its type. This serves to exclude a blemished animal, because other animals of its type are sacrificed on the altar.
messages.lead: Rather, Rava again retracted his previous answer and said:

notes.dh: לאפוקי בעל מום דאיכא דקרב במינו [דליכא במינה דקרבה]
notes.he: וכי תקשי לך טרפה נמי איכא במינה דקרבה ודמיא לבעל מום דאיכא במינו דקרב ותקדוש קדושת הגוף [כבעל מום]:
notes.en: To exclude a blemished animal, which has its kind that is sacrificed [unlike one that has no kind that is sacrificed]. And if it is difficult for you: a tereifa too has its kind that is sacrificed, and it is similar to a blemished animal, whose kind is sacrificed, so let it be consecrated with inherent sanctity like a blemished animal:

messages.text: What did you say to challenge this explanation? You said that in the case of a tereifa, there are other animals of its type that are sacrificed, and if so, why doesn’t inherent sanctity rest upon a tereifa? The answer is that a tereifa is not similar to a blemished animal, as a non-kosher animal is forbidden for consumption, and a tereifa is forbidden for consumption. This serves to exclude a blemished animal, which is permitted for consumption.
messages.quote: what will you say about a tereifa, as other animals of its type are sacrificed

notes.he: מאי אמרת טרפה איכא נמי במינה לא דמיא לבעל מום דבהמה טמאה אסורה באכילה וטרפה אסורה באכילה לאפוקי בעל מום דמותר באכילה - כלומר אי לא מדמיא טרפה לטמאה להא מילתא דיש במינה קרב דמיא לה במילתא אחריתי דאסורה באכילה כמותה:
notes.en: What did you say, that a tereifa also has its kind? It is not similar to a blemished animal, for a non-kosher animal is forbidden for consumption and a tereifa is forbidden for consumption, to exclude a blemished animal, which is permitted for consumption: that is to say, even if a tereifa is not compared to a non-kosher animal in this matter, since its kind is sacrificed, it is compared to it in another matter, that it is forbidden for consumption like it.

notes.he: טרפה לבעל מום להאי עניינא דבעינן למימר אלא דמיא לבהמה טמאה דמה בהמה טמאה אסורה באכילה אף טרפה אסורה באכילה [ולא] (הילכך לא) קדשה קדושת הגוף כבהמה טמאה לאפוקי בעל מום דמותר באכילה (הילכתא) [הילכך קדיש] קדושת הגוף:
notes.en: It is not similar: a tereifa to a blemished animal in this matter that we want to say. Rather, it is similar to a non-kosher animal: just as a non-kosher animal is forbidden for consumption, so too a tereifa is forbidden for consumption, and it is not consecrated with inherent sanctity, like a non-kosher animal. To exclude a blemished animal, which is permitted for consumption; therefore it is consecrated with inherent sanctity.

messages.caption: Why Rabbi Elazar’s animals are “like a non-kosher animal”: Rav Pappa’s comparison, the challenges from a blemished animal, a tereifa and “too long or closed”, and where Rava ends up.

messages.text: One who consecrates an animal that is a tereifa is required to wait until it develops a permanent blemish, on account of which he may redeem it.
messages.lead: § With regard to a tereifa:

notes.he: דקסבר שמואל נחתא לה קדושת הגוף:
notes.en: It requires a permanent blemish, etc.: for Shmuel holds that inherent sanctity takes effect on it.

notes.he: אם רוצה לפדותה:
notes.en: It requires a permanent blemish to be redeemed on its account: if he wishes to redeem it.

messages.text: Since the meat of a tereifa is unfit for consumption and may only be fed to the dogs, why does it require redemption? Should one learn from this that one redeems sacrificial animals in order to feed them to the dogs? But this is contrary to the accepted halakha (see 31a).
messages.quote: is required to wait until it develops a permanent blemish

notes.he: ואנן קי"ל (לקמן תמורה לא.) דאין פודין את הקדשים להאכילן לכלבים אלא למיתה:
notes.en: Conclude from it, etc.: but we hold (below, Temurah 31a) that one does not redeem sacrificial animals to feed them to dogs; rather, [they are left] to die.

messages.text: If one consecrates an animal that is a tereifa, it becomes sanctified until it is time for the animal to die, so that even after its death it must be buried and may not be redeemed.
messages.lead: Rather, say that the statement of Shmuel was as follows:

notes.he: שהרי היא אינה ראויה לאכילת אדם דטרפה היא ואינה ראויה אלא לכלבים אלא עושה קדושה למות. דאינה בר פדיה אלא כונסין אותה לכיפה והיא מתה מאליה כלומר דנחתא לה קדושת הגוף:
notes.en: Conclude from it that one redeems sacrificial animals to feed them to dogs: for it is not fit for human consumption, since it is a tereifa, and is fit only for dogs. Rather, it becomes sanctified to die: it is not subject to redemption; rather, one puts it into a chamber and it dies of itself. That is to say, inherent sanctity takes effect on it.

messages.text: The printed Aramaic here carries a passage in parentheses: “one who thinks it is permitted to consecrate blemished animals for the altar: with regard to a substitute, it is consecrated; with regard to sacrificial animals, it is not consecrated.” The Davidson English leaves it out.

If one consecrates an animal that is a tereifa, this is like nothing other than one who consecrates mere wood and stones, which cannot become sanctified with inherent sanctity but only for their value, and which therefore can be redeemed. Consequently, a consecrated tereifa animal may be redeemed even if it is going to be fed to the dogs.

notes.he: ונפדים ליאכל לכלבים דלאו קדשים מקרייא:
notes.en: Like one who consecrates wood [Rashi’s heading adds, in parentheses, “and sulfur,” where the daf reads “and stones”]: and they are redeemed to be fed to dogs, for they are not called sacrificial animals.

notes.dh: ופליגא דר' אושעיא דאמר המקדיש טרפה הוי כמתפיס עצים ואבנים בלבד
notes.he: כלומר דקדושת דמים [היא]. טעמא משום דהקדישה ואח"כ נטרפה:
notes.en: And this disagrees with Rabbi Oshaya, who said: one who consecrates a tereifa is like one who dedicates wood and stones alone; that is to say, it is sanctity of value. The reason [the mishna rules that one may not redeem them] is that he consecrated it and afterward it became a tereifa.

messages.text: We learned in a mishna (31a):
messages.lead: The Gemara raises a difficulty against the opinion of Shmuel.

messages.text: With regard to all sacrificial animals that became tereifa, one may not redeem them and render them non-sacred, because their consumption is forbidden; and one does not redeem sacrificial animals to feed them to the dogs.

The reason that they may not be redeemed is because they became tereifa after they had already been consecrated. Consequently, if they were already tereifa from the outset, when they were consecrated, one may redeem them.
messages.quote: all sacrificial animals that became tereifa, one may not redeem them

messages.text: Perhaps this tanna holds that anywhere that an animal itself is not fit for sacrifice, inherent sanctity does not rest upon it at all.

notes.he: ואיבעית תימא לעולם נעשו קא תני וקא דייק הא היו טרפה פודין האי תנא סבר כל היכא כו':
notes.en: Or if you wish, say: it actually teaches “that became,” and one infers from it that if they were tereifa [from the outset] one may redeem them; this tanna holds that anywhere, etc.

messages.text: Rashi reads the next challenge first, before the one from the mishna of sacrificial animals that became tereifa, and has Rabbi Eliezer where the daf has Rabbi Elazar; Rabbeinu Gershom’s notes follow the same order.
Another challenge to Shmuel’s opinion from the mishna. Come and hear, as

notes.he: הכי גרסינן מיתיבי ר' אליעזר כו' הך גרסי' ברישא והדר הך כל הקדשים שנעשו טרפה:
notes.en: This is how we read: “They raised an objection: Rabbi Eliezer [the daf reads Rabbi Elazar] says, etc.” This we read first, and afterward that one: “All sacrificial animals that became tereifa.”

messages.text: An animal crossbred from diverse kinds, and a tereifa, and an animal born by caesarean section, and a tumtum animal, and a hermaphrodite animal are not sacred through consecration and they do not sanctify non-sacred animals by means of substitution.

They are not sacred with regard to substitution, i.e., if one said that any of these animals should be a substitute for a sacrificial animal it does not become sanctified; and they do not sanctify non-sacred animals, i.e., if one of these types of animal was sanctified and one attempted to render a non-sacred animal a substitute for it, that non-sacred animal does not become sanctified.
messages.lead: And Shmuel says in explanation:

messages.text: But since they do not become sanctified, how can they sanctify another non-sacred animal? Rather, you find the ruling of Rabbi Elazar applies only when one sanctifies an animal and afterward it becomes a tereifa.
messages.lead: And it is taught in a baraita that

notes.he: דקדשה קדושת הגוף:
notes.en: You find: that it is consecrated with inherent sanctity.

messages.text: This indicates that if it was a tereifa from the outset, then inherent sanctity does not rest upon it; this ruling contradicts the opinion of Shmuel, who says that such an animal must be buried when it dies.

notes.he: קודם שהקדישה לא קדשה קדושת הגוף:
notes.en: But if it was a tereifa from the outset: before he consecrated it, it is not consecrated with inherent sanctity.

notes.he: האי תנא ר' אלעזר כל דלא חזיא להקרבה לא קדיש קדושת הגוף וש"מ סבר דלא קדשה קדושת הגוף ותיובתא דשמואל דאמר (דקדשה קדושת הגוף דקדושת מת) [עושה קדושה] למות היינו קדושת הגוף [קסבר אע"ג דלא חזי להקרבה הא היו מעיקרא שהיו טרפה קודם שהקדישן פודין אלמא לא קדשה קדושת הגוף] תני היו טרפה מעיקרא אין פודין אותן:
notes.en: He holds: this tanna, Rabbi Elazar, holds that whatever is not fit for sacrifice is not consecrated with inherent sanctity. Conclude from it that he holds it is not consecrated with inherent sanctity, and this is a refutation of Shmuel, who said “it becomes sanctified to die,” which is inherent sanctity. [On the mishna:] he holds that even though it is not fit for sacrifice, if they were tereifa from the outset, before he consecrated them, one may redeem them; evidently it is not consecrated with inherent sanctity. Teach [instead]: if they were tereifa from the outset, one may not redeem them.

messages.text: Shmuel could have said to you: Perhaps this tanna also holds that anywhere that an animal is not fit itself for sacrificing, inherent sanctity does not rest upon it. Shmuel himself holds in accordance with those who disagree with this opinion.

notes.he: קסבר ר' אליעזר כל היכא דלא חזיא כו' ואנא דאמרי כרבנן:
notes.en: Shmuel can say to you: Rabbi Eliezer [the daf reads Rabbi Elazar] holds that anywhere it is not fit, etc., and I, who said [my ruling], hold in accordance with the Rabbis.

notes.he: הא מני דקתני הא הוו מעיקרא פודין ר"א היא:
notes.en: Perhaps: whose view is this, which teaches “but if they were so from the outset, one may redeem them”? It is Rabbi Eliezer’s [the daf reads Rabbi Elazar].

notes.he: הדרן עלך יש בקרבנות
notes.en: We will return to you, Yesh BaKorbanot.

messages.text: הדרן עלך יש בקרבנות · Hadran alakh Yesh BaKorbanot: we will return to you, chapter 2, “There Are among the Offerings.”
Chapter 3 · אלו קדשים · Elu Kodashim: sacrificial animals whose offspring and substitutes share their status, beginning with the peace offering.
Mishna

These are the sacrificial animals for which the halakhic status of their offspring and substitutes is like their own halakhic status: The offspring of peace offerings, and their substitute animals, and even the offspring of their offspring or their substitute animals, and even the offspring of their offspring, until the end of all time [ad sof kol ha’olam].

notes.he: אלו:
notes.en: These: [the heading of Rashi’s note on the new mishna; no comment follows it.]

notes.he: אלו קדשים (שלמים) שוולדותיהן ותמורותיהן כיוצא בהן [קרבן] קריבין וולד שלמים ותמורתן וולד וולדן של שלמים עד סוף כל העולם דינן כשלמים (דאמרת את) [שמעינן לר"א דאמר] וולד שלמים לא יקרב שלמים אלא ירעה:
notes.en: These are sacrificial animals whose offspring and substitutes are like them: they are sacrificed. The offspring of peace offerings and their substitute, and the offspring of the offspring of peace offerings, until the end of all the world: their law is like peace offerings. We heard that Rabbi Elazar said: the offspring of a peace offering is not sacrificed as a peace offering, but rather grazes.

messages.text: They are all endowed with the sanctity and halakhic status of peace offerings, and therefore they require placing hands on the head of the animal, and libations, and the waving of the breast and the thigh in order to give them to the priest.
Gemara
Since the tanna already taught: The offspring of the offspring or the substitute and the offspring of their offspring, why do I need him to state: Until the end of all time?
messages.quote: until the end of all time

notes.he: ל"ל למיתני עד סוף העולם:
notes.en: And since it taught “their offspring and the offspring of their offspring”: why do I need it to teach “until the end of the world”?

messages.text: The tanna of our mishna heard that Rabbi Elazar said in the next mishna that the offspring of a peace offering is not sacrificed as a peace offering, but rather it is sequestered and left to die,

notes.he: במתני' ולד שלמים לא יקרב אלא ימות:
notes.en: He heard Rabbi Eliezer [the daf reads Rabbi Elazar], who said: in the mishna, the offspring of a peace offering is not sacrificed, but rather is left to die.

messages.text: @Rabbi Elazar It is not necessary to state with regard to their offspring that I do not concede to you, as I maintain that it is sacrificed upon the altar as a peace offering, but even with regard to all of the offsprings until the end of time I do not concede to you, as I rule that they are all sacrificed as peace offerings.
messages.lead: and the tanna of our mishna said to him:

notes.dh: לא מיבעיא בוולדות דלא מודינא לך אלא אפילו עד סוף העולם לא מודינא לך
notes.he: וא"ת ליתני עד סוף העולם ולא ליתני ולדן וולד ולדן וי"ל דלא זו אף זו קתני שכן דרך משנה לשנויי הכי ותימה דבריש הכותב (כתובות פג:) בעי פירי פירות דווקא או עד סוף העולם דווקא או תרווייהו דוקא והכא לא הוה בעי הכי וי"ל דהתם בלישנא הכתוב בשטר דייקי דאין לכתוב בשטר דבר שאינו צריך אבל בלישנא דמתני' ליכא למידק כולי האי ובריש מס' יבמות (דף ב.) לא דייק כיון דתנא צרותיהן וצרות צרותיהן עד סוף כל העולם למה לי כדדייק הכא דפשיטא ליה דכולהו צריכי למיתני דלא (הוה ליה למימר) דפטרי צרות וצרות דצרות אי לאו דתנא להו לכולהו:
notes.en: It is not necessary to say with regard to the offspring that I do not concede to you; rather, even until the end of the world I do not concede to you: And if you say: let it teach “until the end of the world” and not teach “their offspring and the offspring of their offspring”? One can say that it teaches “not only this but also this,” for that is the way of the Mishna, to teach in this manner. And it is puzzling, for at the beginning of HaKotev (Ketubot 83b) the Gemara asks whether “produce of the produce” is precise, or “until the end of the world” is precise, or both are precise, and here it does not ask so. One can say that there they are exacting about wording written in a document, since one should not write in a document something that is unnecessary, but in the wording of the Mishna there is no need to be so exacting. And at the beginning of tractate Yevamot (2a) the Gemara is not exacting, as it is here, to ask: since it taught “their rival wives and the rival wives of their rival wives,” why do I need “until the end of the world”? For it is obvious to it that all of them needed to be taught, since we would not have known that rival wives and the rival wives of rival wives are exempt had it not taught all of them.

notes.he: לא מיבעיא וולדן דקרב שלמים כו':
notes.en: It is not necessary [to say] that their offspring is sacrificed as a peace offering, etc.

messages.text: § With regard to the mishna’s statement that the halakhic status of the offspring of peace offerings and their substitutes are like that of the peace offering itself: From where are these matters derived? As the Sages taught in a baraita:

“And if his offering be a sacrifice of peace offerings: If he offer of the herd, if male if female, he shall offer it without blemish before the Lord.” Since the verse already states: “If he offer of the herd,” the words “if male if female” are unnecessary. Rather, the word “male” serves to include the offspring of a peace offering as having the same halakhic status as a peace offering.

verse.he: וְאִם־זֶבַח שְׁלָמִים קׇרְבָּנוֹ אִם מִן־הַבָּקָר הוּא מַקְרִיב אִם־זָכָר אִם־נְקֵבָה תָּמִים יַקְרִיבֶנּוּ לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה׃
verse.en:
If your offering is a sacrifice of well-being uncertain.—
If you offer of the herd, whether a male or a female, you shall bring before GOD one without blemish.

notes.he: גבי שלמים שנאמר ואם זבח שלמים קרבנו וגו' והוה ליה למיכתב אם מן הבקר הוא מקריב תמים יקריבנו אם זכר אם נקבה למה לי אי לאו לדרשה:
notes.en: “Male”: concerning peace offerings, as it is stated: “And if his offering be a sacrifice of peace offerings,” etc. The verse should have written: “If he offer of the herd, he shall offer it without blemish.” Why do I need “if male, if female,” if not for exposition?

notes.he: היינו קרא דכתיב אם זבח שלמים קרבנו אם מן הבקר הוא מקריב אם זכר [אם נקבה]. דלא אצטריך (נקבה) אם זכר אם נקבה כיון דאמר מר אם מן הבקר סתם [הוי] משמע בין זכר בין נקבה (וקרא) [אלא] להכי אצטריך זכר לרבות את הוולד ונקבה לרבות התמורה:
notes.en: “If male”: this is the verse that is written: “And if his offering be a sacrifice of peace offerings: if he offer of the herd, if male, if female.” For “if male, if female” was not needed, since it said “of the herd” without qualification, which implies both male and female. Rather, it was needed for this: “male” to include the offspring and “female” to include the substitute.

messages.text: But could this not be derived through an a fortiori inference: If a substitute of a peace offering, which is lenient in that it is not grown from consecrated property, i.e., it is not the offspring of a sacrificial animal, is sacrificed as a peace offering, then with regard to the offspring of a peace offering, which is more stringent since it is grown from consecrated property, is it not logical that it be sacrificed as a peace offering?

notes.he: כדמרבי בסמוך מנקבה:
notes.en: Is sacrificed: as is included shortly from “female.”

notes.he: ולכתוב נקבה ולא אצטריך למכתב זכר לצורך וולד דמצי יליף וולד מתמורה מק"ו:
notes.en: Let it write “female,” and it would not need to write “male” for the sake of the offspring, for one could derive the offspring from the substitute by an a fortiori inference.

notes.he: ולילף תמורה מוולד ולא מיבעי קרא והלא דין הוא כו':
notes.en: “But could this not be derived,” etc.: and let us derive the substitute from the offspring, and a verse would not be needed: “But could this not be derived,” etc. [Rabbeinu Gershom also runs the inference the other way, from offspring to substitute.]

messages.text: This a fortiori inference may be refuted: What is unique about the halakhic status of a substitute? It is unique in that the halakha of substitution applies to all sacrificial animals that belong to an individual, and therefore the substitute of a peace offering is offered as a peace offering.

notes.he: קדשי יחיד:
notes.en: In all sacrificial animals: offerings of an individual.

messages.text: Shall you say the same with regard to the offspring, which is more lenient in that it does not apply to all sacrificial animals, as some are male and do not give birth, and therefore there is reason to say that it is not sacrificed as a peace offering, since the halakha with regard to the sanctity of the offspring does not apply to all sacrificial animals?

notes.he: דהא עולה ואשם זכרים נינהו:
notes.en: The offspring does not apply in all sacrificial animals: for a burnt offering and a guilt offering are males.

notes.dh: מה לוולד שכן גידולי הקדש תאמר כו'
notes.he: להכי אצטריך למיכתב תרווייהו זכר ונקבה:
notes.en: “What about the offspring, which is grown from consecrated property; shall you say,” etc.: for this reason it was necessary to write both, “male” and “female.”

messages.text: Therefore, the verse states the word “male” to include the offspring, and it states the word “female” to include the substitute of a peace offering, indicating that both have the status of a peace offering.

notes.he: ואף על גב דכתיב (ויקרא כ״ז:י׳) והיה הוא ותמורתו יהיה קדש אצטריך קרא לרבויי דקרבה וא"ת מאי שנא דהכא איצטריך קרא לרבויי דקרב וגבי בכור ומעשר כתיב הם דממעטינן מיניה הכא ולא וולדות ולא תמורתו וי"ל אחרי שכתוב מיעוט גבי בכור ומעשר אצטריך הכא קרא לרבות:
notes.en: “Female” to include the substitute: And even though it is written (Leviticus 27:10): “Then both it and that for which it is changed shall be holy,” a verse was needed to include that it is sacrificed. And if you say: what is different, that here a verse was needed to include that it is sacrificed, while with regard to the firstborn and the tithe “they” is written, from which we exclude: [they,] and not their offspring nor their substitute? One can say: since a restriction is written with regard to the firstborn and the tithe, a verse was needed here to include.

messages.text: I have derived only that the substitute of an unblemished peace offering and the offspring of an unblemished peace offering have the status of a peace offering. From where do I derive that the offspring of blemished animals and the substitute of blemished animals which are themselves unblemished have the status of peace offerings? The verse states in a more expanded form: “If male,” to include the offspring of blemished animals, and “if female,” to include the substitute of blemished animals.

notes.he: שהאם תמימה:
notes.en: And the offspring of unblemished animals: whose mother is unblemished.

notes.he: לרבות:
notes.en: “If”: to include.

notes.dh: וולד בעלי מומין ותמורת בעלי מומין מנין דקרבי
notes.he: בעל מום שקדם הקדשו את מומו שעושה תמורה כדאמרינן טוב מעיקרא עושין תמורה:
notes.en: From where do we derive that the offspring of blemished animals and the substitute of blemished animals are sacrificed: a blemished animal whose consecration preceded its blemish, which effects substitution, as we say: what was good from the outset effects substitution.

notes.he: כשהוא אמר אם מאם אם קא מירבו:
notes.en: When it says “if”: from “if,” “if,” they are included.

messages.text: @Abaye But why should I not reverse the interpretations and say that the words “if male” serve to include the substitute of blemished animals, and the words “if female” serve to include the offspring of blemished animals?
messages.quote: “If male,” to include the offspring of blemished animals, and “if female,” to include the substitute of blemished animals

notes.he: אם זכר לרבות תמורת בעלי מומין אם נקבה לרבות ולד בעלי מומין:
notes.en: And I will reverse: “if male” to include the substitute of blemished animals, and “if female” to include the offspring of blemished animals.

messages.text: It stands to reason that from the same place that the substitute of unblemished animals is included, i.e., from the word “female,” the substitute of blemished animals is also included, i.e., from the expanded form “if female.” Likewise, since the word “male” teaches that the offspring of an unblemished peace offering is included, the offspring of a blemished peace offering is included from the phrase “if male.”
messages.lead: Abaye responds:

notes.he: מנקבה איתרבאי תמורת תמימין הלכך מאם דסמיך ליה איתרבאי תמורת בעלי מומין ולא מאם דסמוך לזכר:
notes.en: From the place where it was included: the substitute of unblemished animals was included from “female”; therefore the substitute of blemished animals was included from the “if” adjacent to it, and not from the “if” adjacent to “male.”

messages.text: Did I say to you to reverse the interpretations of the phrases “if male” and “if female”? I actually said that the interpretation of the entire verse should be reversed as follows: Say that the word “male” serves to include the substitute of both a blemished and an unblemished offering, and the word “female” serves to include the offspring of both a blemished and an unblemished offering.
messages.lead: Rav Safra said to Abaye in explanation of his question:

notes.he: זכר לרבות תמורה ואם דידיה לתמורת בעלי מומין נקבה לרבות ולד ואם דידיה לולד בעלי מומין:
notes.en: The whole verse: “male” to include the substitute, and its “if” for the substitute of blemished animals; “female” to include the offspring, and its “if” for the offspring of blemished animals.

notes.he: א"ל רב פפא מי קאמינא לך ליפוך אם אם אנא כוליה קרא קאמינא לך דליפוך והכי קא אמינא אם זכר לרבות את התמורה ואם דידיה לרבות בעלי מומין ונקבה לרבות את הוולד ואם דידיה לרבות וולד בעלי מומין. א"ל לא מצית אמרת הכי דוולד לשון זכר משמע להכי מיתרבי מזכר ותמורה לשון נקבה משמע להכי מיתרבי מאם נקבה] והדין תנא מייתי לה לוולדות (נמי מקרי קדש ומהכא) ולתמורות [מן הדין קרא:
notes.en: Rav Pappa [the daf reads Rav Safra] said to him: Did I say to you to reverse “if,” “if”? I am speaking of reversing the whole verse, and this is what I say: “if male” to include the substitute, and its “if” to include blemished animals; and “female” to include the offspring, and its “if” to include the offspring of blemished animals. He said to him: you cannot say so, for “offspring” implies a masculine form, so it is included from “male,” and “substitute” implies a feminine form, so it is included from “if female.” And this tanna brings it, for the offspring and for the substitutes, from this verse:

messages.text: It is logical to interpret the verse as the baraita does, as the word offspring [valad] indicates a masculine form, while the word substitute [temura] indicates a feminine form.
messages.lead: Abaye said to him in response:

notes.he: הלכך מזכר נפקא:
notes.en: Indicates a masculine form: therefore it is derived from “male.”

messages.caption: “If male, if female” (Leviticus 3:1): what each word includes in the baraita, Rav Safra’s proposed reversal, and Abaye’s answers.

messages.text: For what matter is that halakha relevant?
messages.lead: § The baraita stated that the offspring of a blemished peace offering has the status of a peace offering.

notes.he: קדשי הנך וולדות של בעלי מומין דהא אמן לא חזיא ליקרב:
notes.en: For what halakha: are these offspring of blemished animals consecrated? For their mother is not fit to be sacrificed.

messages.text: It is relevant with regard to sacrificing it on the altar as a peace offering, even though its mother is blemished and disqualified for the altar. And the baraita is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Elazar, who rules that if one sets aside a female animal for a burnt offering, and that animal gave birth to a male, the offspring is offered as a burnt offering, even though its mother may not be offered as a burnt offering (see 18b).
messages.quote: For what matter is that halakha relevant?

notes.he: דאמר במתני' הפריש נקבה לעולה וילדה ולדה קרב עולה אע"ג דאימיה לא חזיא הכא נמי קרבי ואע"ג דאימיה לא חזיא ואצטריך לאשמועינן הכי:
notes.en: And according to Rabbi Elazar: who said in the mishna: If one set aside a female for a burnt offering and it gave birth, its offspring is sacrificed as a burnt offering, even though its mother is not fit. Here too, they are sacrificed even though their mother is not fit, and it was necessary to teach us this.

notes.he: ליקרב ואליבא דרבי אלעזר (ואפי' אליבא דרבי אלעזר) דאמר במתני' המפריש נקבה לעולה וילדה זכר ירעה הוולד עד שיסתאב ואף האם שאין דין להביא עולה נקבה ר' אלעזר אומר (הוא) [הולד] עצמו יקרב עולה דמהו דתימא כי אמר ר' אלעזר הוולד יקרב עולה היכא דאיכא שם עולה על אמו שהרי מצינו עולה בנקבה [בעופות] בעולת העוף [דאמרינן דאין תמות וזכרות בעופות דיכול להביא עולת עוף נקבה אבל הני וולדות ותמורות בעלי מומין דאין שם שלמים על בעלי מומין אימא דקסבר ר' אלעזר דלא קרבי] קמ"ל (דאפי') ר' אלעזר נמי סבר דקרבו כמו וולד עולה. ורבנן פליגי עליה דירעו:
notes.en: To be sacrificed, and according to Rabbi Elazar, who said in the mishna: One who sets aside a female for a burnt offering and it gave birth to a male, the offspring shall graze until it becomes blemished, and so too the mother, since it is not right to bring a female burnt offering; Rabbi Elazar says: the offspring itself shall be sacrificed as a burnt offering. For lest you say: when Rabbi Elazar said that the offspring is sacrificed as a burnt offering, that is where the name of burnt offering applies to its mother, for we find a female burnt offering among birds, in the bird burnt offering, as we say that unblemished status and maleness are not required in birds, so one may bring a female bird burnt offering; but these offspring and substitutes of blemished animals, where the name of peace offering does not apply to blemished animals, say that Rabbi Elazar holds they are not sacrificed. It teaches us that Rabbi Elazar too holds that they are sacrificed, like the offspring of a burnt offering. And the Rabbis disagree with him, [holding] that they graze. [A printer’s note here suggests reading: “It teaches us that even with the substitute of blemished animals Rabbi Elazar holds that they are sacrificed.”]

messages.text: The baraita therefore teaches that the same is true with regard to the offspring of a blemished peace offering. And although Rabbi Elazar already stated this principle, it was necessary for the baraita to repeat it in this case, lest you say that when Rabbi Elazar says his opinion, it is only with regard to a burnt offering, due to the fact that there the discrepancy between mother and offspring is their sex, and there is burnt offering status for females, i.e., the case of a bird that is the same sex as its mother, as one may sacrifice a female bird burnt offering.

notes.he: התם הוא דאמר רבי אלעזר גבי עולה דאיכא שם עולה על אמן כלומר דאע"ג דהיא עצמה לא קרבה לא פקעה קדושה מינה שהרי מצינו נקבה עולה כגון עולת העוף דאין תמות וזכרות בעופות:
notes.en: Lest you say: it is there that Rabbi Elazar said so, with regard to a burnt offering, since the name of burnt offering applies to its mother; that is to say, even though she herself is not sacrificed, sanctity does not depart from her, for we find a female burnt offering, such as a bird burnt offering, since unblemished status and maleness are not required in birds.

notes.he: פרש"י כלומר דנקבה שייכא בעולה שהרי מצינו עולת נקבה בעולת העוף דאין תמות וזכרות בעופות אבל גבי וולדות שלמים דבעלי מומין דאין שם קדשים על אמן דלא מצינו בעל מום קרב שלמים דהא שלמים עוף ליכא עכ"ל בר פדא אמר לרעיה ואליבא דדברי הכל דאפי' רבי אליעזר דאמר גבי מפריש נקבה לעולה וילדה הוא עצמו יקרב עולה היינו טעמא משום דאיכא שם עולה על אמו פירוש בעולת העוף וקשה לפרש"י דא"כ דמהני שם עולת העוף דשייכא באם להולד אם הפריש נקבה בעלת מום לעולה וילדה היה לנו לומר דהולד עצמו קרב עולה דהא איכא שם עולת העוף על אמו ומשמע דממעט כל ולד בעלי מומין ועוד דלקמן משמע דלא מהני שם עולה דעוף דאם לולד ונראה לה"ר מ"ר לפרש דאיכא שם עולה על אמו כלומר דקדושה קדושת הגוף אם הפריש נקבה וילדה דאין לה פדיון ומש"ה דין הוא שיקריב הולד עצמו אבל בעלי מומין דליכא קדושת הגוף עלייהו כלל אין דין הוא שיקרב הולדות אלא ירעו הרמ"ר מורי:
notes.en: Since the name of burnt offering applies to its mother: Rashi explained: that is to say, a female belongs to [the category of] burnt offering, for we find a female burnt offering in the bird burnt offering, since unblemished status and maleness are not required in birds; but with regard to the offspring of blemished peace offerings, the name of sacrificial animals does not apply to their mother, for we do not find a blemished animal sacrificed as a peace offering, since there is no peace offering of birds. End of his words. [On this reading:] “Bar Padda said: for grazing, and according to all,” for even Rabbi Eliezer, who said that one who sets aside a female for a burnt offering and it gave birth, the offspring itself is sacrificed as a burnt offering, his reason is that the name of burnt offering applies to its mother, meaning in a bird burnt offering. And this is difficult for Rashi’s explanation: for if so, that the name of bird burnt offering that applies to the mother is effective for the offspring, then if one set aside a blemished female for a burnt offering and it gave birth, we should say that the offspring itself is sacrificed as a burnt offering, since the name of bird burnt offering applies to its mother; yet it implies that it excludes every offspring of blemished animals. Furthermore, below it implies that the mother’s [status as a] bird burnt offering is not effective for the offspring. And it seems right to my teacher, the Rav M. R. [abbreviated in the text], to explain “the name of burnt offering applies to its mother” as meaning that she is consecrated with inherent sanctity when one set aside a female and it gave birth, for she has no redemption; therefore it is right that the offspring itself be sacrificed. But blemished animals, on which there is no inherent sanctity at all, it is not right that their offspring be sacrificed; rather, they should graze. [So] my teacher, the Rav M. R.

messages.text: But perhaps these offspring of a blemished peace offering are not sacrificed, as there is no case of a blemished animal that may be offered as a peace offering. Therefore, it teaches us that even these offspring may be sacrificed.

notes.he: שלמים בעלי מומין דאין שלמים על אמן דלא מצינו בעל מום קרב שלמים דהא שלמים עוף ליכא אימא לא קרבי:
notes.en: But with regard to the offspring: of blemished peace offerings, where the name of peace offering does not apply to their mother, for we do not find a blemished animal sacrificed as a peace offering, since there is no peace offering of birds, I would say that they are not sacrificed.

messages.text: The statement of the baraita that the offspring of a blemished peace offering has the status of a peace offering is relevant only with regard to grazing the animal until it develops a blemish, after which it may be redeemed and the money used to bring a burnt offering. But the animal itself may not be sacrificed on the altar. And the baraita is in accordance with all opinions.
messages.quote: For what matter is that halakha relevant?

notes.he: דאפילו רבנן מודו דקדשי מיהא לרעייה ולא אמרי' חולין נינהו דהא אמרינן נמי גבי עולת נקבה ולדה ירעה:
notes.en: According to all: for even the Rabbis concede that they are at least consecrated for grazing, and we do not say that they are non-sacred, since we also say with regard to a female burnt offering that its offspring shall graze.

notes.he: אימא דלא ליקרב קמרבי אלא לרעייה ואתיא אליבא דדברי הכל בין לרבנן בין לר' אלעזר דעד כאן לא קאמר ר' אלעזר בוולד עולה דיקרב משום דאיכא שם עולה על אמו אבל הני לא. אימא איפכא דמאם זכר מרבי תמורות בעלי מומין ומאם נקבה מרבי וולד בעלי מומין אמר ליה מיסתברא מהיכא דמיתרבי וולד תמימין מן זכר מן תמן מן אם דידיה מיתרבו (תמורת) [וולד] בעלי מומין ומן היכא דאיתרבו תמורת תמימה מנקבה מן אם דידיה מיתרבו תמורת בעלי מומין:
notes.en: Bar Padda said: say that it includes them not to be sacrificed but only for grazing, and it accords with all opinions, both the Rabbis and Rabbi Elazar; for Rabbi Elazar said only with regard to the offspring of a burnt offering that it is sacrificed, since the name of burnt offering applies to its mother, but not these. Say the reverse: that from the “if” of “male” the substitutes of blemished animals are included, and from the “if” of “female” the offspring of blemished animals are included. He said to him: it stands to reason that from where the offspring of unblemished animals is included, from “male,” from there, from its “if,” the offspring of blemished animals are included; and from where the substitute of an unblemished animal is included, from “female,” from its “if” the substitutes of blemished animals are included. [Rabbeinu Gershom’s order places this exchange after bar Padda’s statement.]

messages.text: As it was stated that the following amora’im disagreed about the same point as did Shmuel and bar Padda:
The offspring of a blemished offering is consecrated with regard to sacrificing it upon the altar, and this is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Elazar.
This halakha applies only with regard to grazing, and this is in accordance with all opinions.

But this tanna cites the source of this halakha from here: “Only the holy things you have, and your vows, you shall take and go to the place which the Lord shall choose; and you shall offer your burnt offerings, the flesh and the blood, upon the altar of the Lord your God; and the blood of your sacrifices shall be poured out against the altar of the Lord your God, and you shall eat the flesh.”
messages.lead: § In the baraita, the halakha governing the substitute and offspring of a peace offering is derived from the superfluous words “male” and “female.”

verse.he: רַק קׇדָשֶׁיךָ אֲשֶׁר־יִהְיוּ לְךָ וּנְדָרֶיךָ תִּשָּׂא וּבָאתָ אֶל־הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר־יִבְחַר יְהֹוָה׃ וְעָשִׂיתָ עֹלֹתֶיךָ הַבָּשָׂר וְהַדָּם עַל־מִזְבַּח יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ וְדַם־זְבָחֶיךָ יִשָּׁפֵךְ עַל־מִזְבַּח יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ וְהַבָּשָׂר תֹּאכֵל׃
verse.en: But such sacred and votive donations as you may have shall be taken by you to the site that GOD will choose. You shall offer your burnt offerings, both the flesh and the blood, on the altar of the ETERNAL your God; and of your other sacrifices, the blood shall be poured out on the altar of the ETERNAL your God, and you shall eat the flesh.

messages.text: With regard to the words: “Only your holy things,” these are the substitutes; “that you have,” these are the offspring. And with regard to these, it states: “You shall take and go to the place which the Lord shall choose,” i.e., they must be brought to the Temple as offerings.

notes.he: רק קדשיך אלו התמורות דתמורה נמי איקרי קדש]:
notes.en: “Only your holy things”: these are the substitutes, for a substitute too is called holy.

notes.dh: אשר יהיו לך משמע אלו הוולדות
notes.he: שעתידות לילד מן הקדשים דמדקאמר קרא תשא ובאת אל המקום ולא יותר שומעני מאחר שנשאם שם אינו צריך לעשות יותר אלא יכניסם לבית הבחירה וימנע מהם מים ומזון כדי שימותו ויפטר:
notes.en: “That you have” implies: these are the offspring, which will be born from the sacrificial animals. For since the verse says “you shall take and go” to the place and nothing more, I would understand that once he has brought them there he need not do more, but may bring them into the Temple and withhold water and food from them so that they die, and be exempt.

messages.text: One might have thought that one should bring them into the Temple but withhold water and food from them so that they die. Therefore, the verse states: “And you shall offer your burnt offerings, the flesh and the blood, upon the altar of the Lord your God.”

notes.dh: יכול יכניסנו לבית הבחירה וימנע מהן כו'
notes.he: דהא איקיים ליה תשא ובאת:
notes.en: One might have thought that one should bring it into the Temple and withhold from them, etc.: for then “you shall take and go” has been fulfilled.

notes.dh: ועשית עולותיך ודם זבחיך ישפך וגו'
notes.he: (דברים י״ב:כ״ז) והאי קרא סמיך לרק קדשיך:
notes.en: “And you shall offer your burnt offerings … and the blood of your sacrifices shall be poured out,” etc. (Deuteronomy 12:27): and this verse is adjacent to “only your holy things.”

messages.text: This indicates that in the manner that you treat a burnt offering, you should treat the substitute of a burnt offering, and in the manner that you treat a peace offering, you should treat the offspring of a peace offering and the substitute of a peace offering.

notes.he: ועשית עולותיך הבשר והדם כדרך שאתה נוהג בעולה. לזרוק דמה ולהקטירה כליל כך אתה נוהג בתמורתה וכדרך שאתה נוהג בשלמים כך אתה נוהג בוולדן ובתמורתן סמיכה ונסכין ותנופת חזה ושוק דכתיב ודם זבחיך ישפך והבשר תאכל יכול אף וולד כל הקדשים יהו להן דין (זה) [אימן]:
notes.en: The verse states, adjacent to it: “And you shall offer your burnt offerings, the flesh and the blood”: in the manner that you treat a burnt offering, to sprinkle its blood and burn it entirely, so you treat its substitute; and in the manner that you treat peace offerings, so you treat their offspring and their substitute: placing hands, libations and the waving of the breast and thigh, as it is written: “And the blood of your sacrifices shall be poured out … and you shall eat the flesh.” One might have thought that the offspring of all sacrificial animals too would have the law of their mothers.

messages.text: One might have thought that this is the halakha with regard to all sacrificial animals, i.e., that their substitutes and offspring are sacrificed upon the altar. Therefore, the verse states: “Only your holy things,” which, as the Gemara will explain shortly, excludes certain offspring from this principle. This is the statement of Rabbi Yishmael.

notes.he: יהא נמי ולדו ותמורתו קרב:
notes.en: One might have thought that all sacrificial animals too: that their offspring and their substitute are also sacrificed.

notes.he: ולקמיה מפרש הי ולד קא ממעט. כל אכין ורקין מיעוטין:
notes.en: The verse states “only”: and below it explains which offspring it excludes. All occurrences of “akh” and “rak” are restrictions.

notes.he: (למעט דין זה וכל שאר וולדות ותמורת) [מיעט וולדי שאר] קדשים:
notes.en: The verse states “only”: it excluded the offspring of other sacrificial animals.

messages.text: The word “only” is unnecessary, as it states with regard to a guilt offering: “It is a guilt offering; he is certainly guilty before the Lord.” The term “It is [hu],” indicates that only it, the guilt offering itself, is sacrificed upon the altar, but its substitute is not sacrificed.

verse.en: It is a reparation offering; they have incurred guilt before GOD.

notes.he: ללמוד מן רק למעט וולדות ותמורת של שאר קדשים מהכא מצית יליף]:
notes.en: Rabbi Akiva says: it is not necessary to learn from “only” to exclude the offspring and substitutes of other sacrificial animals; you can derive it from here:

notes.he: הוא עצמו קרב ולא תמורתו וכן נמי תמורת שאר קדשים. הא מהיכא תיתי דיהא רשאי למנוע מהן מזון כדי שימותו והא כיון דגמירי כו' הידין ולד מצי אמר בשאר קדשים דקרב:
notes.en: “It is a guilt offering”: it itself is sacrificed, but not its substitute, and so too the substitute of other sacrificial animals. [On the Gemara that follows:] From where would this come, that he would be permitted to withhold food from them so that they die? But since we learned, etc. Which offspring could you say, of the other sacrificial animals, is sacrificed?

messages.text: Due to the phrase in the verse “You shall take and go,” one might have thought that one should bring the substitute and offspring into the Temple but withhold water and food from them so that they die. Therefore, the verse states: “And you shall offer your burnt offerings, the flesh and the blood, upon the altar of the Lord your God.”
messages.lead: § The Master said above:
messages.quote: One might have thought that one should bring them into the Temple but withhold water and food from them so that they die

messages.text: From where would this be derived, that these animals should be brought into the Temple and then left to die? Since the halakha that five sin offering are left to die is learned through a tradition transmitted to Moses from Sinai, and the offspring of a sin offering and the substitute of a sin offering are included among those five, it would have been reasonable to conclude that only those sin offerings are left to die, but these animals, the offspring of a peace offering and the substitute of a peace offering, are sacrificed upon the altar.

notes.he: דתיסק אדעתיה דימותו דאצטריך עולותיך וגו' הא ודאי כיון דגמרינן ה' חטאות מתות תרי מינייהו ולד חטאת ותמורת חטאת מכלל דולד שלמים ותמורת שלמים לא מייתי דהא לא גמירי אלא בחטאת:
notes.en: From where would it come: that it would enter your mind that they should die, so that “your burnt offerings,” etc., was needed? Certainly, since we learn that five sin offerings die, two of them being the offspring of a sin offering and the substitute of a sin offering, by implication the offspring of a peace offering and the substitute of a peace offering do not come to that, for it was learned only with regard to a sin offering.

messages.text: The verse is necessary, lest you say that these five sin offerings may be left to die in any location, but these, the offspring and substitute of a peace offering, must be left to die specifically in the Temple. Therefore, the verse teaches us that this is not so, as the offspring and substitute of a peace offering may be offered upon the altar.

One might have thought that this is the halakha even with regard to all sacrificial animals that their substitutes and offspring may be sacrificed upon the altar just as the sacrificial animals themselves are. Therefore, the verse states: “Only your holy things,” indicating that this principle does not apply equally in all cases.
messages.lead: § The master said above:
messages.quote: One might have thought that this is the halakha with regard to all sacrificial animals

messages.text: The offspring of which offering is referred to here? If it is referring to the offspring of a burnt offering, a burnt offering is male, and is therefore not capable of giving birth. And if it is referring to the offspring or substitute of a sin offering, it is learned as a tradition that such an animal is left to die.

notes.he: ולאו בר אולודי הוא ואי תמורה דידיה ודאי קרבה ואי דאשם הלכתא גמירי לה דלרעייה אזלא הוא הדין דהוה מצי למימר זכר הוא ולאו בר אולודי הוא כמו גבי עולה אלא ניחא ליה למיפרך ממילתא אחריתי וא"ת לפר"ת דאמר הלכה למשה מסיני כל שבחטאת מתה באשם [קרב] עולה אמאי לא מוקי לה באשם וי"ל דבהא לא מצי לאוקומי דפשיטא ליה דאינו קרב באשם ורק משמע דממעט ליה דאינו קרב בקדשים דאתי מיניה ולהכי לא אצטריך דפשיטא הוא דאינו קרב באשם:
notes.en: If of a burnt offering, it is male: and is not capable of giving birth; and as for its substitute, it is certainly sacrificed. And if of a guilt offering, it is learned as a halakha that it goes to grazing. The same holds that it could have said “it is male and not capable of giving birth,” as with a burnt offering, but it preferred to raise the difficulty from another matter. And if you say: according to Rabbeinu Tam, who said that it is a halakha transmitted to Moses from Sinai that wherever with a sin offering the animal dies, with a guilt offering it is sacrificed as a burnt offering, why does it not establish [the baraita] as referring to a guilt offering? One can say that it could not establish it so, since it is obvious to it that it is not sacrificed as a guilt offering, and “only” implies that it excludes it from being sacrificed as the kind of offering it comes from; therefore it was not needed, for it is obvious that it is not sacrificed as a guilt offering.

messages.text: Continued on 18a: and if it refers to the substitute of a guilt offering, that too is learned as a tradition: it goes out to graze. The Gemara then looks for what “only” excludes.
